noise_summary: 193 results filtered as off-topic across four main categories. (1) Australian politics (~30 items): extensive coverage of Tony Abbott elected Liberal Party federal president, Angus Taylor vs. Labor, One Nation polling, teal independents party speculation, and Victorian political donations — all from Australian outlets about Australian domestic politics. (2) African CAF (Confederation of African Football) (~22 items): Mamelodi Sundowns CAF Champions League victory, AFCON U-17 semi-finals and final, club licensing deadlines, World Cup squad announcements for African nations — appearing in results because search queries for 'CAF' (Canadian Armed Forces) also retrieved the African football body. (3) French CAF (Caisse d'Allocations Familiales) (~22 items): French social welfare payment schedules, fraud cases, housing authority partnerships, and benefit calculation guides — appearing because 'CAF' queries returned the French family allowance agency. (4) Other international / non-Canada content (~119 items): foreign-language articles from Spanish, Turkish, Catalan outlets citing CSIS (US think tank, not Canadian Security Intelligence Service) on US missile stockpiles and Iran war; Indian CISF (Central Industrial Security Force) stories; French lifestyle/astrology articles from grazia.fr and claudeleveque.com where 'Joly' is an author surname; PSG Champions League celebrations covered by French radio ici.fr; karting race results featuring competitor 'Lucas Joly'; Spanish newspaper Grupo Joly business articles; Nigerian NDP (National Democratic Party) candidate announcements; US opinion pieces about conservatism; NATO/Romania drone strike stories with no Canadian actor involvement; sports articles about Canada's World Cup squad (player injury, tournament atmosphere) unrelated to political actors; and various other lifestyle, recipe, and local community news items from French and Spanish publications triggered by actor surname searches.

stories.headline: Carney delivers 'new partnership' pitch to US business leaders at Economic Club of New York
stories.summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney travelled to New York on Thursday to address the Economic Club, calling for a new Canada-US economic partnership premised on mutual strength and continental integration. Employing Trump's own slogan, he said 'Canada strong will help make America great again,' a shift in tone from his earlier rhetoric about reducing dependence on the US, and highlighted cooperation potential on critical minerals, energy, and manufacturing supply chains.

stories.headline: Alberta separation referendum triggers national debate over Clarity Act, Carney-Smith tensions, and Quebec reaction

stories.headline: Canada enters technical recession as Poilievre demands emergency parliamentary debate
stories.summary: Statistics Canada reported Friday that GDP contracted 0.1% annualized in Q1 2026, following a revised 1.0% decline in Q4 2025, marking what some economists call a technical recession — Canada's first since the pandemic. Conservative Leader Pierre Poilievre sent an open letter to Carney calling for an emergency parliamentary debate, filed a non-binding motion blaming Liberal policies, and labelled Canada the only G7 nation in recession; the Liberals moved to fast-track a second budget bill in response.

stories.headline: Guilbeault resigns as Liberal MP over Carney government's climate policy backsliding

stories.headline: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi visits Ottawa in first such trip in a decade, hints at trade doubling
stories.summary: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi arrived in Ottawa for a three-day visit — the first by a Chinese foreign minister in ten years — meeting Foreign Affairs Minister Anita Anand and Prime Minister Carney. Wang Yi dangled the possibility of doubling bilateral trade and declared a 'stable and constructive partnership' was being built. stories.headline: Canada's Big Six banks post strong Q2 earnings, beating forecasts despite mounting insolvencies
stories.summary: Canada's six largest banks reported second-quarter results for the period ending April 30, collectively beating analyst expectations with profit growth of 10-25% year-over-year. Royal Bank posted net income of $5.5 billion, up 25%; TD reported a rise driven by interest income; Scotiabank CEO cited the Carney government's business-friendly approach as attracting investors. Despite the strong results, household insolvency volumes rose approximately 26% and analysts questioned whether the earnings represented a peak.

stories.headline: CSIS watchdog finds intelligence service failed to adequately report possibly illegal employee conduct to minister
stories.summary: The National Security and Intelligence Review Agency released a report covering 2024 that found CSIS may have violated the law by failing to fully inform the public safety minister of potentially illegal conduct by employees, including possible Charter violations. The watchdog said the CSIS director's annual report did not adequately reflect the extent of legal issues, with CSIS having reported only three such cases to the minister since 2017.
